_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
Running work keeps a finished subagent row and opens its conversation. The test seeded a conversation at /c/rw-statushelper. "The strip" is '[aria-label="Running work"]', "the toggle" is its [data-testid="running-work-toggle"], and "the row" is the strip's ".running-work-agent".
1. Navigate to /c/rw-statushelper and wait up to 30s for [data-testid="message-input"] to be visible.
2. Fill the message input with "subagent: statushelper bash: sleep 120" and click [data-testid="send-button"].
3. The toggle should come to contain "statushelper" (wait up to 30s). Click the toggle.
4. The row should contain "statushelper", and come to contain "sleep" (wait up to 30s).
5. Call "cancelSubagent" (cancels the subagent through the API); it should return "ok".
6. The row's ".running-work-agent-time" should come to have exactly the text "Finished" (wait up to 15s). The toggle should still have aria-expanded "true".
7. Click the row. The URL should come to contain "/c/statushelper" (wait up to 10s).
